explanation: What's happened to the sky? On Friday, the photogenic launch plume from a SpaceX rocket launch created quite a spectacle over parts of southern California and Arizona. Looking at times like a giant space fish, the impressive rocket launch from Vandenberg Air Force Base near Lompoc, California, was so bright because it was backlit by the setting Sun.
title: SpaceX Rocket Launch Plume over California

explanation: What's happened to the Milky Way? In terms of human sky watching history, not much -- but in terms of a single exposure image, quite a lot. Featured here is a single 15-second wide-angle exposure of the night sky over Rusinowo, Poland, taken in mid-August.
title: Perseid Meteor, Red Sprites, and Nova RS Ophiuchus

explanation: What causes Venus to have phases? The same reason the Moon has phases -- because both the Moon and Venus orbit the Sun and reflect sunlight from a surface that is always half illuminated by the Sun.
title: Phases of Venus

explanation: What would it look like to see the Earth spin? A time-lapse video composed of images taken by cameras on board the Elektro-L weather satellite answers this question dramatically.
title: Equinox on a Spinning Earth

explanation: Sometimes the sky itself puts on a show. As the Sun dipped below the horizon, energetic particles from the Sun collided with the upper atmosphere of the Earth, producing a beautiful green aurora above a quiet horizon.
title: Aurora Above
